$comment: Which models this deployment is permitted to read labels with. The decision belongs to the IT Systems Administrator role — Marcus Williams in the stakeholder register (SRC-3) — though note that nobody in the brief asked for it: it is derived from D29, which holds that a moving model identifier invalidates every audit record citing it, and from the observation that Google's stable names can be repointed without notice. Recorded here because there is nowhere better yet: D14 leaves the prototype unauthenticated, so a runtime admin surface would be a control with no gate behind it. A file in the repository is at least versioned, diffable and reviewed. An administrative interface is a production-path item (design §15); this becomes its seed, not its replacement.

approvals.rationale: Natively multimodal with tool calling; the first reader wired. Fully qualified, so the identifier cannot move under the audit record (D29).

Second reader, added so B-Q4 can be measured rather than argued. Note the weaker pin: Google retired numbered versions after 2.0, so this is a stable name that can be repointed. The per-job fingerprint exists to make that detectable.
